newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Rules: Sydney, Nth Melbourne in AFL final.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Rules: Sydney, Nth Melbourne in AFL final.

text.p: Star full-forward Tony Lockett on Saturday kicked the Sydney Swans into their first Australian Football League (AFL) grand final when he scored in the final minute of their semifinal against Essendon.
Lockett broke a deadlock when he sent a towering punt 60 metres (200 feet) for a point to give Sydney a one-point win over Essendon, 10.10 (70) to 10.9 (69).
Sydney will now play North Melbourne in next Saturday's grand final after North Melbourne thrashed Brisbane 17.12 (114) to 11.10 (76) earlier in the day.
The grand final will mark the first time Sydney's only AFL team has played a side from Melbourne, the game's traditional heartland, for the AFL pennant.
Lockett missed Sydney's previous two games with a groin injury but took a courageous mark in the final minute of the match against Essendon to give his side a chance of victory.

Lockett's catch was 60 metres from goal and, while he missed the main target for six points, his kick safely made it through the secondary target for a point to end a thrilling match in front of 41,731 fans at the Sydney Cricket Ground.
The Sydney club came into being in 1982 when the financially struggling South Melbourne agreed to move to Sydney rather than face expulsion from the AFL.
Sydney this year topped the AFL standings at the end of regular season matches for the first time, with North Melbourne close behind in second place.
